3
A copper pipe has a true diameter of 42.03 mm.
A builder measures the diameter of the pipe five times using digital calipers. The measurements
are shown.
diameter / mm
48.01
47.99
48.01
48.00
47.99
What describes the builder’s measurements?
A
accurate and precise
B
accurate but not precise
C
not precise and not accurate
D
precise but not accurate

hints: Compare the true diameter of $42.03\text{ mm}$ with the five caliper readings near $48.00\text{ mm}$ and estimate the size of the shift.
Check the spread of the readings from $47.99\text{ mm}$ to $48.01\text{ mm}$ to judge how repeatable they are.
Link small spread to precision and large distance from the true value to accuracy, then combine the two judgements.
walkthrough: Recall the definitions: precise means repeated readings agree closely with each other, accurate means the mean reading is close to the true value of $42.03\text{ mm}$.
Check precision: the readings are $48.01$, $47.99$, $48.01$, $48.00$, $47.99\text{ mm}$, a range of only $0.02\text{ mm}$, so they are highly repeatable.
Check accuracy: the mean is about $48.00\text{ mm}$, which differs from $42.03\text{ mm}$ by about $5.97\text{ mm}$, much larger than the spread.
A large consistent shift with a tiny spread suggests a systematic error such as a zero error on the digital calipers.
Therefore the set is precise but not accurate. This is option D.

A.explanation: The readings cluster tightly but their mean of about $48.00\text{ mm}$ is about $6\text{ mm}$ from the true $42.03\text{ mm}$, so they are not accurate.

B.explanation: The readings are all within $47.99\text{ mm}$ to $48.01\text{ mm}$, so the spread is very small and they are precise, not imprecise.

C.explanation: The range of only $0.02\text{ mm}$ shows high repeatability, so the set cannot be described as not precise.

D.explanation: The five values agree to within $0.02\text{ mm}$ showing precision, but all are far from $42.03\text{ mm}$ showing a systematic error and poor accuracy.
